newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks open higher, Iraq seen weighing mood.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks open higher, Iraq seen weighing mood.

text.p: Stocks opened higher on Thursday on the back of expected expansion of foreign shareholding limit, but brokers said the crisis in the Middle East would depress sentiment, limiting any steep price rises, brokers said.
The composite stock index rose 1.03 points to 792.67 in the first 13 minutes of trading.
"The Iraq crisis has not yet been reflected in the Seoul market because of the news on the limit expansion for foreign investors," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Brokers said another "oil shock" could deal a serious blow to the already faltering economy.
South Korea depends heavily on the Middle East for imports of crude oil.
"Oil price rises is sure to increase the size of the nation's trade deficit and fuel inflationary pressure," said a Hyundai Securities broker.

Brokers said the market would be backed by good news such as the launching of savings scheme for stock investment in October. The finance ministry said earlier it would give tax breaks for workers who want to invest in the stock market through savings accounts with securities houses.
